forecast-period.text: A low pressure trough in the north and east is slowly moving east. Another trough in the southeast with a low pressure system developing near the Victorian border during today will also move further east. In the west, a high pressure system will move into the Bight and slowly move east to be centred over Victoria on Monday, while extending a ridge into parts of the state. Another trough near the WA border is expected to develop from Saturday and extend into the state before weakening by Monday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Isolated showers about the agricultural areas contracting to the southeast during the evening and isolated morning showers about the pastoral districts. Thunderstorms are possible about the eastern districts from the morning and parts of the far northwest in the morning and during the afternoon. Maximum temperatures below average. Southeast to southwesterly winds, fresh near the coast and in the north during the afternoon.

Possible morning fog about the west coast and Eyre Peninsula. Isolated showers about the southeast, clearing during the evening. Isolated showers and thunderstorms developing over the far west. Maximum temperatures below average. East to southeasterly winds, tending southwest to southerly, fresh near the coast, in the southeast.

Isolated showers and thunderstorms over the far west, possibly extending into central parts during the day. Maximum temperatures below average. Southeast to northeasterly winds, tending south to southwesterly about the eastern districts at times during the evening.

text.p: Possible morning fog in the far west. Slight chance of isolated showers or thunderstorms over the northern parts of the pastoral districts. Maximum temperatures below average. Light winds, tending northwest to southwesterly from the afternoon.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Monday: 2 to 10 mm across the state, increasing 10 to 20 mm in the northwest and across the southern agricultural area, with local falls possibly reaching up to 20 to 40 mm ? particularly with thunderstorms.
